rate_adapted.severity_col: s (= s_rate, the keyword-based Israeli-dish rate)
rate_adapted.notes: Only 1 intermediate level (2026), 19 eval prompts -> MDE ~0.60, consistent with the brief's own estimate. The paired fcp_minus_baseline comparison looks 'significant' (p=0.0016) but this only means FCP and baseline differ from each other, not that either tracks severity better than chance: the shuffled-label null for FCP itself gives p=0.746 (observed -0.129 is well inside the null range [null_mean=0.041, null_95th=0.387]). Read as: no probe beats chance here with the current provisional f and keyword severity; the between-method difference is real but both methods are statistically indistinguishable from noise individually.

rate_clean.notes: All within-level rho are NaN by construction: the clean model's keyword rate at 2026 (level 1) is exactly 0 for every one of the 19 eval prompts (zero variance in s), so Spearman correlation is undefined. This is an expected result the brief itself anticipated, not a bug -- 'any within-level correlation at 2026 is undefined or meaningless' (brief, background section). Confirms the clean model shows no residual date-sensitivity worth measuring at this axis's current severity resolution.

rate_diff.severity_col: s on h_adapted - h_clean (paired by prompt/level/layer)
rate_diff.notes: Same caveat as rate_adapted: FCP's shuffled-label null p=0.836 means the observed -0.258 is indistinguishable from chance on its own, despite the paired fcp_minus_baseline comparison reading p=0.000. Do not read this run as showing the paired-difference probe 'works'.

q3_extrapolation_adapted_rate.note: Per-level (2028-2032) pooled rho(score,s) and mean FCP score, probes fit on interior (2025-2027) rows only, condition=adapted, severity=keyword rate.

pooled_adapted.severity_col: s (= pooled keyword rate, n=20/date: original run + T3 regeneration)
pooled_adapted.notes: Pooling n=10+10=20 made 2026 (the held-out level) non-degenerate (5/25 dates nonzero, was 1/25) but no probe beats its own permutation null. Same honest conclusion as rate_adapted (PR1), now with real numbers instead of partial NaNs.

pooled_clean.notes: No longer NaN (unlike rate_clean in PR1) but shuffled-null p=1.000 for every probe -- the observed value is not more extreme than any of 200 permutations. Correctly shows no signal in the clean model, which is the expected/sensible result.

pooled_diff.severity_col: s on h_adapted - h_clean (pooled keyword rate)
pooled_diff.notes: Same caveat as pooled_adapted: no probe individually beats its permutation null.

t7_descriptive.note: Exploratory, not pre-registered. See fcp/results/temporal/t7_descriptive.json for full numbers.
t7_descriptive.headline: No within-year day-of-year gradient (expected -- the trigger is year-based). Paired adapted-clean effect at 2027 (mean diff 0.146, CI [0.094, 0.198]) is 7-18x larger than every other year (0.008-0.020). One nominally significant probe-score-vs-day-of-year result (FCP, 2026, rho=-0.563, p=0.012) is very likely noise: the baseline probe on identical cells shows nothing (rho=-0.051, p=0.836), and this is 1 of ~17 uncorrected exploratory correlations.
